Herb Ellis demonstrates the idea of “minimum effort, maximum results.” His melodic guitar playing has been an integral part of numerous classic jazz recordings, especially with the renown Oscar Peterson Trio of the 1950s. He was born in Texas in 1921, graduated from North Texas State, and found inspiration from Charlie Christian, another Texas guitarist. Previous to joining Oscar Peterson he played with Glen Grey, Jimmy Dorsey and the Soft Winds Trio. Herb often accompanied Ella Fitzgerald and recorded with fellow guitarists Joe Pass, Barney Kessel and Charlie Byrd. He makes his home in Arkansas and can be found at festivals and jazz venues across the country, occasionally with the Tonight Show Alumni Band.
Herb was interviewed by Michael Woods in Los Angeles on September 3, 1995.

We are here today at the Marriott in Los Angeles filming interviews for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. We have with us today one of the world’s most outstanding jazz guitarists, Herb Ellis. Pleased to meet you.
Yes. I wanted to ask you some things about how you got started playing guitar.
